explanation: Malay had been the trading language of the archipelago's ports for centuries. In 1928 young nationalists adopted it as their language of unity, under the name Bahasa Indonesia.

claims.text: Indonesian (Bahasa Indonesia) is a standardized form of Malay.
Indonesian is not a standardized form of Javanese, Dutch or Sundanese.
Malay was a trading language across the ports of the Indonesian archipelago for centuries.
In the Youth Pledge of 1928, young Indonesian nationalists adopted Malay, as Bahasa Indonesia, as their language of unity.

writerNotes: Counterintuitive: Java is Indonesia's best-known island, so Javanese is the obvious pick, and it is wrong. Self-check (CONTENT_GUIDE 9.3), all eleven codes confirmed true. The selfCheck field itself is left out because the CNT-1 item schema refuses it as an unknown key, so the codes are recorded here. lint: content:check reports no errors and no warnings for this item. claims: 4 listed, 2 high (checker_doubt, date) and 2 standard, every one at or above the C26 floor and raised where a fact is beyond everyday knowledge. datasets: mledoze-countries cca3=IDN lists ind (Indonesian) as the official language and cca3=MYS lists msa (Malay); language-codes lists ind and msa separately; none records that one is a form of the other. rivalTest: Argued for Javanese, the language of Java, as hard as I could: Indonesian grew from Malay, though it has borrowed many Javanese and Dutch words. Sundanese is another language of Java. c1's risk reason is checker_doubt, standing in for counterintuitive, which the tooling's enum lacks. The item replaces an Equatorial Guinea item that repeated p.geo.0249. volatility: evergreen, a settled fact that cannot change; no time words, and nothing rests on knowledge newer than mid-2026. regional: the foothold is the Malay of neighbouring Malaysia, Brunei and Singapore. style: Oxford spelling, straight single quotes, plain hyphens only, explanation of 28 words. myths: every claim screened against content/reference/myths.json; no entry matches. mystery and encore: nothing of either kind in a practice item. doubts: none.
